analysis.title: Beyond the Noise - Monthly market perspectives November 2026
key_insights: Vontobel stays constructive on equities and expresses the overweight through emerging market stocks. October brought new all-time highs but more volatility from oil near $100 on Iran tensions, a tech selloff on AI financing doubts and Chinese chip competition, and hot inflation that forced a Fed hike.

Global monetary easing has run its course and many central banks, including the Fed, are hiking or preparing to. Vontobel expects the tightening cycle to be short-lived because inflation is supply-driven and not demand-driven, and calls market pricing of almost three more Fed hikes by next summer overly aggressive.

Growth accelerated in 2026 on the AI investment boom and earlier rate cuts. Vontobel expects momentum to peak in coming quarters as high oil prices and elevated short and long yields tighten financial conditions and fiscal support fades into 2027.

Inflation is elevated from stacked supply shocks (US tariffs, chip shortage, Iran war). Vontobel sees peak supply-driven impact as probably reached, with effects fading through 2027, and limited risk of a 2021-22 style second wave. 5y5y inflation expectations remain stable and cyclical core PCE has not picked up.

Four key 2027 risks: monetary overtightening, a fiscal sustainability crisis (US, France, UK), an AI capex crisis, and another geopolitical supply shock. Vontobel's AI-top checklist shows model progress, adoption and capex guidance still positive, while hyperscaler free cash flow has turned negative for many, off-balance-sheet debt is rising and CDS is high, especially for Oracle.

Fixed income: at the October Investment Committee Vontobel cut high yield from overweight to neutral and raised government bonds from underweight to neutral, adding duration ahead of an expected softer 2027. Corporate investment grade stays underweight because of tight spreads and heavy AI-related issuance, with hyperscalers a large share of supply running above the 2021-25 average.

Vontobel believes longer-dated yields have likely peaked and notes that after Trump's first term the 2018 midterms marked a 10-year yield peak, suggesting a gridlock result could do the same. EM hard-currency bonds stay neutral on solid fundamentals but rich valuations.

FX: USD should stay supported near term by Fed repricing and French political risk weighing on the euro, but Vontobel sees a rates-driven bounce and not a structural bull market. It expects EUR/USD in a 1.10-1.15 range and CHF to stay well supported by safe-haven flows, with limited further gains because of the SNB and the yield disadvantage.

Gold stays overweight despite pressure from higher real yields and a stronger dollar in the fall. Vontobel admits its calls for a weaker USD and a less hawkish Fed were wrong for now, and cites central bank buying, ETF inflows, fiscal deficits and geopolitics as structural support.

Commodities stay neutral as risks are expected to ease ahead of the US midterms and Middle East oil supply gradually returns. Brent should stay firm in H1 2027 on inventory rebuilding and tight refined products, then fall as exports recover. Insurance-linked securities are favored as a decorrelated return source.

Sector calls: Positive on communication services, financials and health care. Neutral on consumer discretionary, energy, industrials, IT, materials and utilities. Negative on consumer staples and real estate.

Communication services is favored for multiple AI monetization paths via cloud, inference, advertising and applications. IT is neutral because growth is concentrated in semiconductors and dispersion is rising, with a preference for AI infrastructure and semis, select software and cybersecurity over traditional IT services.

Financials are positive after a sell-off driven by positioning and long-end yields, with revisions breadth turning positive and ECM and DCM strong. Energy is neutral because oil is already above $100 and EPS downgrades could follow a strong first half, while valuations and free cash flow argue against a bearish view.

Consumer staples are negative on volume weakness, private labels, retailer bargaining power and GLP-1 adoption with demanding valuations. Real estate is negative with 30-year mortgage rates above 7%. Materials face a deteriorating China credit impulse, so Vontobel prefers industrial gases and specialty materials over bulk commodities.
The US midterm replay notes Democratic majorities in both chambers, implying more reliance on compromise on budget matters, with US debt above $40 trillion and Q3 GDP growth at 3.4% annualized.

Vontobel promotes a Momentum Strategy Index family (US, Switzerland, EMU) with a long leg of top momentum stocks rebalanced quarterly and a short index futures leg activated when strategy volatility passes its 90th percentile, offered as tracker certificates with a 0.75% annual management fee.

sector_views.rationale: Large search and social advertisers can monetize AI across cloud, inference, advertising and applications, and cloud revenue should increasingly offset capex.
Spending is resilient but energy costs, inflation and housing affordability constrain purchasing power. Valuations have corrected and bearish positioning could be contrarian if oil recedes.
Growth has been price-driven with weak volumes. Private labels, retailer pricing power and GLP-1 adoption squeeze margins while valuations remain demanding.
Earnings are strong but oil above $100 limits incremental upside and EPS downgrades could follow. Valuations and free cash flow argue against a bearish view.
The sell-off reflected positioning and long-end yields, not fundamentals. Revisions breadth is positive, capital markets are strong and credit growth is supportive.
Defensive earnings, GLP-1 driven volume growth and AI adoption make it an uncorrelated complement to the AI trade.
Higher yields and oil above $100 caused a cyclical sell-off. Orders and backlogs are improving but the earnings recovery is uneven and Q3 results are a catalyst.
AI infrastructure demand is strong but growth is concentrated in semiconductors. Dispersion, not sector-wide demand, is the key issue.
A sharp deterioration in China's credit impulse and higher energy costs limit earnings acceleration. Prefers industrial gases and specialty materials.
30-year mortgage rates above 7%, weak builder confidence and commercial property challenges with no AI demand catalyst. Best treated as a funding source.
Electrification and AI power demand are offset by heavy upfront capex, rate sensitivity and regulators resisting cost pass-through amid political pressure over electricity bills.

earnings_insights: Vontobel says corporate earnings are holding up well and AI-linked investment remains strong, supporting its equity overweight.
Energy sector earnings show resilient demand, solid margins and cost discipline, though EPS downgrades could come after a strong first half.
IT earnings momentum is strong but concentrated in semiconductors. IT EPS growth falls by roughly half to the mid-20% range when semiconductors are excluded.
Financials earnings revisions breadth has turned positive and health care earnings revisions are rising while the sector's performance has lagged.
Industrials Q3 results are flagged as a key catalyst, with the earnings recovery described as uneven.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Energy-driven inflation is the main issue. Hot inflation data forced the Fed to hike in October.
Growth is robust but unevenly distributed, with high living costs and interest rates straining households.
The Fed has resumed hiking. Vontobel expects the cycle to be short-lived.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed rate hikes priced by markets
macro_indicators.reading: almost three additional hikes by next summer
macro_indicators.interpretation: Vontobel views this as overly aggressive given supply-driven inflation.
Yields hit multi-decade highs and retreated from peaks late in October. Vontobel sees them as likely peaked.
Elevated on Iran and Strait of Hormuz disruptions. Vontobel expects gradual normalization in 2027.
Weighs on housing and real estate valuations.
Inflation eases but does not normalize as supply effects fade.
Vontobel's view is in line with consensus per the forecast table.
Pressured by real yields and the dollar. Vontobel sees the pressure as temporary.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight equities via emerging market stocks
trade_ideas.rationale: Relative valuation, a weaker USD over time, domestic fiscal stimulus and exposure to the AI capex boom, with North Asian exporters benefiting from AI hardware demand.
trade_ideas.risk: Stronger US dollar, elevated US yields, weakness in Korean and Taiwanese semiconductors and growing tech concentration in the index.

trade_ideas.rationale: Central bank buying, ETF inflows, fiscal deficits and geopolitical tension, with a limited and short tightening cycle.
trade_ideas.risk: Rising real yields and a stronger dollar, which Vontobel admits it misjudged.

trade_ideas.rationale: Tight spreads, heavy AI-related issuance and higher inflation.

trade_ideas.description: Government bonds upgraded from underweight to neutral and high yield cut from overweight to neutral
trade_ideas.rationale: Government bond yields at multi-decade highs offer returns without credit risk, adds duration ahead of softer 2027 growth and inflation, and high yield struggles as growth slows.
trade_ideas.risk: Elevated inflation risks and further yield increases.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight insurance-linked securities as a decorrelated alternative
trade_ideas.rationale: Investments with decorrelated returns are favored amid high economic and political uncertainty.

risk_factors: Monetary overtightening by central banks ending the cycle.
Fiscal crisis if markets challenge US, French or UK fiscal sustainability.
AI capex cycle ending through overinvestment, a Chinese technological breakthrough, negative hyperscaler free cash flow or excessive hyperscaler leverage.
Another global supply shock from the Iran war, Ukraine war or Strait of Hormuz disruptions.
Fading global fiscal stimulus in 2027 as most of the ten largest economies consolidate.
Higher mortgage rates, consumer loan costs and funding costs weighing on housing, consumption and investment.
Rising AI-related corporate bond issuance pressuring investment grade spreads.
Concentration of EM indices in technology keeping volatility elevated.
China credit impulse deterioration weakening industrial demand.

vol_and_positioning: Retail investor sentiment (bulls minus bears) is cautious rather than greedy despite strong equity markets this year.
Consumer discretionary positioning is increasingly bearish with negative flows, which Vontobel sees as potentially contrarian if oil prices recede.
IT positioning is cleaner after the summer correction, but September showed IT as the only sector to rise, so positioning is less helpful short term.
EUR positioning is already bearish, which Vontobel says contains downside.
Vontobel's equity market top checklist tracks melt-up, mega-IPOs, crowded positioning, tighter financial conditions and weakening revisions, noting two or three signals can be enough to mark a top.
Historically the S&P 500 tends to see initial weakness around the first Fed hike, with returns turning positive relatively soon after (7 episodes since 1990).
The Momentum Strategy Index activates its short index futures leg when strategy volatility passes the 90th percentile of the past 252 days and deactivates it at the 80th.
geopolitical: Iran war and Strait of Hormuz supply-chain disruptions keep oil near $100 and are a key upside risk to prices.
French budget and political uncertainty drive the euro's risk premium and safe-haven flows into the Swiss franc.
US midterm elections with Democratic majorities in both chambers, implying more compromise and possible fiscal gridlock.
Rising Chinese competition in semiconductors triggered a selloff in Korean and Taiwanese chip stocks.
Ukraine war listed among possible sources of another global supply shock.
US tariffs cited as one of the supply shocks behind elevated inflation, with trade relations an ongoing uncertainty.

tension_points.bull_case: Exponential model improvement continues, adoption is rising, hyperscalers regularly raise capex guidance, cloud margins are improving and most hyperscalers still hold net cash.
tension_points.bear_case: Free cash flow has turned negative for many hyperscalers, off-balance-sheet debt is rising, Oracle CDS is high, AI bond issuance is heavy and a Chinese technological breakthrough could undercut the capex case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Hyperscaler capex guidance stops increasing, free cash flow stays negative, or markets challenge hyperscaler leverage. Vontobel says two or three checklist signals can already be enough to mark a top.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation is supply-driven, cyclical core inflation has not picked up and expectations are stable, so the tightening cycle is short-lived and yields have likely peaked.
tension_points.bear_case: Markets price almost three more Fed hikes by next summer, resilient labor markets reduce policy urgency and oil near $100 keeps headline inflation elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A stronger labor market keeping the Fed hawkish would extend the cycle. Vontobel expects the next job market weakness to end the tightening.

tension_points.bull_case: A gridlock result could mark the peak in 10-year yields, as in the 2016-2020 path.
tension_points.bear_case: Record debt above $40 trillion, rising interest costs and fiscal sustainability concerns could keep yields elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gridlock that lets Democrats block fiscal stimulus unless the economy moves into recession is the scenario assumed. A fiscal crisis would break it.

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation is supply-driven, so the renewed tightening cycle should be brief and market pricing of three more hikes is too aggressive.
theme_stances.evidence: we expect the renewed tightening cycle to prove relatively short-lived

theme_stances.key_argument: The AI capex cycle remains intact despite headwinds from fading fiscal stimulus and tighter financial conditions.
The EM pullback is a reset, with North Asian exporters benefiting from AI hardware demand and relative valuation support.
theme_stances.evidence: we view the recent pullback as a reset rather than a change in trend
